featured_reviews.name: Priyadarshini Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I found Vriksha Nursery on Instagram. I was especially bedazzled by their collection, but what impressed me was the effort they seemed to take in caring for these plants. That is how I ended up purchasing my first set of plants from them: a Calathea White star, a Calathea Rosetopia, a Calathea Rattlesnake, a Persian Shield and  a Watermelon Remustasia (I may have gotten the spellings wrong) in July 2020. The plants arrived in excellent condition and looked beautifully healthy and well groomed. They also sent plant care information (unfortunately I didn't follow their guidance well and ended up harming 3 of my plants). I continued to enquiry about the care and update (via WhatsApp) and withing 24 hours, received proper guidance.

In November, I visited the heavenly nursery for the first time (after making a appointment) and was spellbound by the plant haven they have created, especially in Mumbai. As expected, the nursery was hustling and bustling with a million things. While maintaining the rules of social distancing, the entire team patiently answered all my questions, showed me every plant I asked about and even looked at photos of my home to suggest the right plant for the right area. I took two plants to them since they weren't doing well, and they helped me with that too. Shaan and Savita were warm, friendly with a quick sense of humour (they were at work and wanting to wrap up as early as possible and go get their dog back from the spa 😊) I bought 4 new plants this time: a Brasil plant, a Fiddle leaf fig, a Croton Mammy and a Dracena Colorama), 3 bags of soil and a plant care spray.

I continue to send them enquiry questions about my plants, and even today, they have continued to help me care for my plants, without expecting any form of compensation. This was especially helpful when I nearly killed my Watermelon Remustasia 😑

I have taken the time to write this review, incorporating my personal experience with the staff at the nursery mainly because of the mixed bag of reviews one read on Google (about the place). I read them too, but decided to experience the place for myself. I waited for a few months before I wrote the review to really see how true or untrue the words online were. I cannot speak for others, and I don't ask to be believed, but for what it's worth, I strongly recommend building a relationship with Vriksha Nursery. As an amateur plant parent, I feel blessed to have found Shaan, Savita and Vriksha Nursery. They're hardworking, creative and passionate people who are genuinely invested in caring for plants, irrespective of who's home the plants are living in.

Thank you Shaan, Savita and Vriksha Nursery for making helping make my home a warm, fresh and inviting place ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Farzan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I honestly don't go anywhere else when buying things for my garden. This is a proper family run, old school nursery, not a corporate garden centre.
Shaan, Sarita and their staff are so knowledgeable and friendly. The staff here know what they're talking about and are always happy to offer advise. At first I thought the plants were on the expensive side but once I bought them I knew they were the best quality and really amazing ones. Special mention to the Kashmiri Custure Roses which have never stopped blooming, the herbs like curry leaves, lemon grass and Rosemary. Their delivery is super fast and I usually receive them at max within a day or two.
Vriksha Nursery really is a hidden gem.

featured_reviews.name: Hozefa Sadriwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vrishka nursery at Vile parle is a different world of greenery! You name it (plants), they have it!
It's a one stop shop for plants for home decor, office decorations, party or corporate giftings, beautification etc.

They have a number of different plants which are available at a affordable rates. Succulents starts from Rs. 350 with a normal pot and goes up to Rs.700.
They have ceramic pots of different colours, size and shape which are available in addition to the crops with the smallest size starting from Rs.200.
They have different types of plants, with different variety in colour updated every week depending on the availability and demand, so you can expect so see voltaile and new flowers & plants, almost everytime you visit the outlet.

The owner guides us through the options available very smoothly and gives amazing suggestions through her in depth knowledge of plants. They offer delivery for the same, but it's expensive. It's open from 10.30 to 6.00 everyday of the week.

featured_reviews.name: Nandkumar Mayanak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an absolutely fantastic Malvani seafood lunch at Malwani Aswad in Vile Parle East. The best part about this place is how close the flavours are to authentic homemade Malvani/Konkani food, rich, fresh, and 100% true to the cuisine. The menu has a huge variety, and it’s rare to find places serving premium fish like Chonak, depending on availability of course.
We started with Tisrya Sukha, and it was bursting with flavour — fleshy clams and a sukha masala that was an absolute banger. The Bombil Fry, Chonak Fry, and Prawns Fry were all incredibly fresh and perfectly fried. The Surmai curry was beautifully balanced, and the Solkadhi paired wonderfully with the meal. Had it all with bhakri and a little rice, and the portions were very generous.
The restaurant is small, but spotlessly clean, very well maintained, and clearly run with a lot of passion. You may have to wait during peak hours, but it is 100% worth the wait. Special shoutout to the owners for serving such authentic flavours with consistency and care. Wishing you bigger success ahead  truly one of the best Malvani food experiences in Mumbai. 🌊🐟🔥

featured_reviews.name: Nisikant Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Gajalee recently for seafood, and the experience was mixed. While the restaurant has a strong reputation and offers a wide variety of seafood (including crab, pomfret, oysters, and even snails), the pricing feels significantly inflated for what is essentially a standard dining setup.

For instance, crab was quoted at around ₹5000 per kg (pre-processing), and a medium-sized pomfret fry, recommended by the staff—cost about ₹2000. The taste was decent, but not proportionate to the premium pricing.

The restaurant tends to be overcrowded in the evenings, likely due to limited seafood options in the surrounding area, drawing local seafood enthusiasts. However, compared to coastal cities like Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata, or Kochi, the prices here are almost double without a corresponding difference in quality or experience.

Overall, it may appeal to those specifically seeking seafood in this locality, but in terms of value for money, it falls short.
N.B: After having Pomfret, I have been suffering from stomach upset (Food poisoning) and currently recovering.
